statements.action_statement: No fixed release is available yet; update when Docker Hardened Images publishes one.
statements.status_notes: CVE-2023-31437 describes an attacker who can already write to a sealed systemd journal file changing its lookup structures (entry arrays and hash tables) so that some views of the journal leave out sealed entries while journalctl --verify still passes. The research behind it is at https://github.com/kastel-security/Journald/blob/main/journald-publication.pdf (section 5.3). The CVE record notes that the systemd maintainers reportedly denied that any of the findings was a security vulnerability, and Debian rates it unimportant with no fix in any release, listing every release up to and including sid as vulnerable: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2023-31437 . No systemd commit or pull request addresses this CVE. A dispute is not a fix, so the status follows the shipped code. Every published build of this package is systemd 257.13 (Debian 257.13-1~deb13u1), built with Forward Secure Sealing enabled: on amd64 and arm64, every published systemd package's journalctl offers --setup-keys and --verify-key, and every published libsystemd-shared package's libsystemd-shared-257.so carries the journal verifier and names libgcrypt.so.20, which it opens at run time for sealing and verification. The sealing and verification code the report concerns therefore ships unchanged. Exploiting it needs write access to the journal files themselves.
